The circuit contains 7 IC's and is divided into three different areas. IC6 and IC7 are the shift registers that serially shift in the twelve bits from the transmitter and parallel outputs the data to a display device.

IC2 is a 555 timer that is used to generate the clock for the entire circuit. IC1 (J-K flip-flop), IC3 (counter), and IC5 (three input NAND gates) are used to control the operation of the circuit, system timing.

A HIGH input to the receiver circuit sets IC1 which enables the shift registers and the counter to count. The counter produces the clock pulses to the shift registers and twelve data bits are shifted in. On the thirteenth count, the flip-flop is reset, and the shift registers are disabled resetting the counter.

The first HIGH into the receiver should be the start pulse shifting in the correct data. If the first HIGH is not the start pulse, the DATA OK and PARITY LEDs will probably give an incorrect indication, meaning the data received is bad.
